SubTopics: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
Content: Read the paragraphs from the passage.

:ibox:In order to make sure the balloon continues to float, the air is heated by burners. The burners are filled with propane which is the same fuel used in outdoor gas grills. Just like a grill, the propane is lit and burns right beneath the opening at the bottom of the balloon. That flame heats the air inside the balloon and makes it rise into the air. The balloon's pilot must turn the burner on and off to heat the air. In this way, the pilot makes the balloon move up and down. But how does a hot air balloon move from side to side?

Hot air balloons travel on natural air currents. An air current is a flow of air over the earth. We feel air currents as wind on our faces. All around the world, air flows in different directions. These currents flow in layers above the earth. Sometimes one current will flow east, but the current above it will flow west. A hot air balloon pilot uses the burner to lift the balloon into different currents. The balloon moves east, west, north, or south depending on the current it's in.
How does the author's use of these paragraphs add to the reader's understanding of air movement? Make `bbtext(two)` choices.

A.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand that moving air feels hot.

B.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand how to move hot and cold air.

C.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand the use of propane gas to move air.

D.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand that hot air balloons travel on currents.

E.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand how hard it is for the pilot to fly a balloon.

F.Choice: The paragraphs help the reader understand the role the pilot plays in moving the balloon.

Content: Read the sentence from the passage.

:ibox:The hot air balloon flies by a `ultext(simple design)`. The balloon is filled with hot air. Hot air weighs less than cold air. So when the hot air is trapped inside of the balloon, the balloon's response is to rise up in the cooler air surrounding it.

A.Choice: It shows that the author believes it is easy to fly a hot air balloon.

B.Choice: It shows that the author thinks that hot air balloons are easy to build.

C.Choice: It shows that the author believes the way a hot air balloon works is easy to understand.

D.Choice: It shows that the author thinks that it is easy to draw hot air balloons before they are built.

SubTopics: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
Content: Liz is writing a story for her class about winning the county spelling bee. Liz wants to revise the story to include a better opening. Read the draft from her story and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:For the last `text(two years)`, I have been the runner-up in the county-wide spelling bee. Both `text(years)` I lost to Aaron Long, but I knew that this was my `text(year)`. I was ready. I had won my school's spelling bee, I had studied long lists of words, and my parents had been calling words out to me for `text(weeks)`. It was a beautiful spring day, and I felt confident. This was going to be my lucky day. There was no doubt that I was going to win this contest.
Choose the `bbtext(best)` beginning sentences to introduce the story.

A.Choice: Spelling bees are great contests. When I was in the fourth grade, I loved getting ready for them.

B.Choice: Winning the county-wide spelling bee was important to me. Spelling was my best subject in school.

C.Choice: Training for a spelling bee is a lot like training for a track meet. You have to work hard to be the best, and the training is hard.

D.Choice: My mouth was dry as I walked into the high school auditorium. It was the day of the county-wide spelling bee, and I wanted to win.

SubTopics: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
Content: A student is writing a report for her teacher about a recent class trip to a local museum. Read the draft of the report and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:Our day at the children's museum started on the first floor, which was about life on Earth. At an exhibit on Earth's history, we dug for fossils in the Dinosaur Dig. Next was a nature display where we listened to bird songs and shook hands with a monkey.

The second floor was all about space. We got to visit a planetarium, a kind of theater that shows the night sky on a high, curved ceiling. We also learned how a telescope works.

We viewed a group of stars called the Milky Way. Looking at the stars helped us understand why someone would want to become an astronaut.
Write an introduction that clearly states the main idea of the report and sets up the information to come in the body of the report.

SubTopics: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
Content: A student has written the draft of an opinion letter to his principal about the school's short recess periods. The student wants to revise the draft to add more support for his opinion. Read the draft of the letter and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:Dear Principal Phillips,

I am writing to ask you to make our recess period longer. `ultext(Twenty-five minutes is just not long enough for students to play.)` By the time we get outside, we have already lost about ten minutes of our time. What time is left does not allow us to play any active games, and we have to hurry back to class. Also, recess is the only time during the day that we can spend with our friends. Having a longer recess would make us better and happier students.

Sincerely,
Blake Hudson
Choose `bbtext(two)` sentences that would add the `bbtext(best)` support to the `ultext(underlined)` opinion about recess.

A.Choice: Most students like to play games such as softball and volleyball.

B.Choice: If we had a longer recess, we would get more exercise and be healthier.

C.Choice: If we had a longer recess, some students could spend some of it studying.

D.Choice: In my brother's high school, the physical education periods are one hour long.

E.Choice: Another problem is that the sports fields are not large enough for baseball and softball.

F.Choice: Students who have more time to be active will be able to think better when they are back in class.

Content: A student made a plan for a research report. Read the plan and the directions that follow.

:box:`ultext(Research Report Plan)`

`bbtext(Topic)`: early American schools
`bbtext(Audience)`: students in social studies class
`bbtext(Purpose)`: to inform
`bbtext(Research Question)`: What were children taught in early American schools?
The student found a source for the research report. Read the source.

:box:In the early days of America, children had many jobs. Boys were expected to help their fathers with the farm work. Likewise, girls were expected to help their mothers with the housework. There wasn't much time for school. Most children who had some time for learning went to a dame school. The name of the school came from the teachers who were called dames. These teachers showed children how to recognize the letters of the alphabet, how to spell, and how to do simple math. If a family could pay for it, some boys had additional schooling from a schoolmaster.

B.Choice: Boys were expected to help their fathers with the farm work.

C.Choice: Likewise, girls were expected to help their mothers with the housework.

D.Choice: There wasn't much time for school.

E.Choice: Most children who had some time for learning went to a dame school.

F.Choice: The name of the school came from the teachers who were called dames.

G.Choice: These teachers showed children how to recognize the letters of the alphabet, how to spell, and how to do simple math.

H.Choice: If a family could pay for it, some boys had additional schooling from a schoolmaster.

SubTopics: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
Content: A student is writing a research report about hovercraft. She found a source. Read Source 1 and the directions that follow.

:ibox:`bbtext(Source 1: Hovercraft by Jane Thomas)`

In `text(1955)`, a British man put some cans and tubes together and made the `text(first)` tiny hovercraft. Hovercraft look like a ship and can float over water, land, or even swamps. They work really well in places where the land is rocky, swampy, or icy because they can float as little as `text(six inches)` or as much as `text(seven feet)` into the air. Hovercraft float because they have big fans that are on the bottom of the craft. The big fans lift them off the ground. This makes hovercraft very useful in places that do not have many roads. In fact, hovercraft are the best way to travel when there are no roads to follow. They are even used to save people when they need help, like during a flood.
The student took notes about hovercraft. Select `bbtext(two)` notes that support the author's opinion in `bbtext(Source 1)`.

A.Choice: Hovercraft are used in many countries in the world.

B.Choice: Hovercrafts are now being used to give tours in many cities.

C.Choice: People who love hovercraft can join clubs and take part in races.

D.Choice: Some hovercrafts are so small that only one person can ride in them.

E.Choice: Hovercraft can help rescue teams get safely to areas where cars cannot travel.

F.Choice: By floating above rocks and waves, hovercraft offer a smooth ride for passengers.
